Example: Bet has a flat base that sticks out to the right; kaf is one smooth curve with no corner. Check the base first.

Hint: A vowel sign is a tiny mark under or beside the letter. Look at its shape and its place before you guess.
Example: Two dots side by side under a letter (tzere) say 'ay'; two dots stacked (shva) are a very short sound or silent.

Hint: Hebrew reads right to left. Start at the right edge of the word and move left, letter by letter.
Example: In שָׁלוֹם start at ש (sh), then ל (l), then ו (o), end at ם (m): sha-lom.

Hint: Alef and ayin carry a vowel but add no consonant sound of their own in everyday Israeli speech.
Example: In אַבָּא only the vowels are heard: a-ba. The first alef just holds the 'a' vowel.

Hint: Five letters change shape at the end of a word. The sound stays the same; only the shape changes.
Example: כ at the start of a word and ך at the end are both kaf: the final one has a long tail down.
